scope: Orchestrator inspection of all eight primary final anonymous bundles, before opening their label mapping. Initial code is scored by the independent reviewers.
limits: The orchestrator previously saw labeled runtime, acceptance and selected source during collection, and early anonymous numeric scores. This is not a fully blinded human assessment. Preferences are qualitative, not calibrated numeric grades. Potential additional boundaries need separate probes.

review-02.notes: B and C are close, direct implementations. A adds descriptor-only input restrictions, a pass-through integer helper and repeated discount validation; extra complexity has no stated product requirement.

review-05.notes: C makes shippingCents non-enumerable, breaking JSON transport and the expected object shape. B treats an explicitly undefined version as absent; distinguish this local-call validation edge from the significant transport defect. A has the clearest complete behavior.

review-07.notes: A records invalid stock/held values but compares quantities before raising, so malformed values combined with real requests can raise TypeError rather than required ValueError. B rejects empty stock dictionaries without a minimum-size requirement. C gates arithmetic behind validation. Repeated valid/invalid bookkeeping makes A/B harder to change.

review-09.notes: All appear adequate on the stated ordinary inputs. B is somewhat more direct; A builds an intermediate validated list and C repeats request iteration. Validation duplication across two small functions is a maintenance consideration, not evidence of a large-system scalability defect.

review-12.notes: Closely similar coherent implementations with exact arithmetic, explicit options and version checks, and ordinary object output. No material design winner established.

review-15.notes: All keep the domain and formatting boundaries small, preserve precision and reject invalid inputs before shipping overrides. Stylistic BigInt/Number choices do not establish better scalability.

review-17.notes: A/B reuse focused validation/aggregation helpers; C reuses reservation for returns, which is reasonable while semantics coincide. C rejects double slashes anywhere in a redirect; the public wording is ambiguous about interior double slashes, so do not count this as a confirmed contract defect.

review-19.notes: The three implementations are nearly equivalent: focused validation, aggregate quantities, checks before applying new copied balances, and a small redirect function. No material maintainability distinction established.
